title: Can a Chatbot Replace the Hotel Phone?
summary: A website chatbot does not pick up the hotel phone. The widget can reply while the published number still rings out. How to check one property in a few minutes.
body_markdown:
Common questions


## FAQ


### Can a chatbot replace the hotel phone?


No. A website chatbot answers guests who open the page. The hotel phone is a number guests call without opening the page. The widget can reply while that number still rings. Replacement would mean the chatbot picks up the number. A window on the site does not.


### Does a website chatbot answer missed calls?


No. A missed call is a ring on the hotel's number that nobody took. The chatbot is not on that number. It can answer a typed message on the site and leave the handset ringing. What the hotel loses when nobody picks up, including after reception closes, is the subject of[the after-hours account](https://www.codyco.ai/blog/what-happens-when-a-guest-calls-your-hotel-after-hours) .


### Why do guests call a hotel that already has a chatbot?


Because the chatbot only meets guests who found it. Many calls are requests the page did not finish: a booking that still needs a last step, a change to an existing stay, an invoice, or a fact that is only true tonight.[The website can look complete and still send the guest to the phone](https://www.codyco.ai/blog/why-guests-still-call-when-everything-is-on-the-website) . The widget sits on that same page.


### Can a chatbot finish a hotel booking?


A chat window can collect details or send the guest onward. On the phone, finishing means a confirmed reservation is in the property management system before the caller hangs up.[Systems that are actually on the line are judged on that test, and many of them stop at a transfer or a message](https://www.codyco.ai/blog/hotel-phone-systems-compared) .


A website chatbot is not on the line, so the test never starts.


### What is the difference between a hotel chatbot and a phone menu?


A phone menu answers the hotel's number and routes the caller. A website chatbot does not answer the number. It waits on the page. Both can leave the request unfinished. The menu at least took the call. The chatbot never joined it.


### How can a hotel check whether its chatbot replaced the phone?


Open the widget and call the published number at the same time, once during reception hours and once after close. If the widget replies and the line rings out, the chatbot did not replace the phone. If the group uses one widget for several properties, run the same check on a second property. One window does not cover a second number.
